newsitem.title: ITALY: STET rises, Telecom falls on merger plan.
newsitem.headline: STET rises, Telecom falls on merger plan.

text.p: Shares in Italian state-controlled telecoms holding company STET rose while Telecom Italia fell after Italian Treasury minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi announced a plan to merge the two companies by May 1997.
By 1545 GMT, STET shares had risen 6.38 percent to 5,685 lire while Telecom Italia was off 7.05 percent at 3,350 lire.

Dealers said that a merger and privatisation would benefit STET, whose privatisation is to be put back to autumn 1997 from early 1997, while dealers said the merger could penalise telecom operator Telecom Italia.
An Italian Treasury statement said Ciampi had instructed Italia. This followed a meeting between Ciampi and European Community Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert in Brussels.
Around 61 percent of STET is held by the Italian Treasury, while STET has a majority holding in Telecom Italia.
